# Queue J stage 2 — J9 notes (branch oc/QO)

## What landed

Protocols **766–773 (1.20.5 – 1.21.10)** now run the **full gameplay path**:
entities, combat, health, hunger, server-driven windows and status effects — not
the old client-trusting subset.

The plan from `QJ-notes.md` § J5 is implemented as a **shared path** rather than
a rewrite of eight codecs:

* `modern::legacy_gen` — generated by `tools/gen/gen_legacy_play.js` from
  PrismarineJS `minecraft-data`: one module per protocol with its packet ids,
  entity types, damage types (in registry order), attribute map, menu ids and
  item data-component ids. The modern field → minecraft-data packet-name aliases
  are derived by matching the checked-in 1.21.11 ids, not by hand.
* `modern::version` gains a [`Gen`](crates/aether-server/src/protocol/modern/version.rs)
  variant per layout era (`V1_20_5`, `V1_21_1`, `V1_21_3`, `V1_21_5`, `V1_21_8`,
  `V1_21_9`, before `V1_21_11`) and a `Version` static for each protocol. The
  old versions take their block states and items from `protocol::compat`
  (substitution included, so a spear is a trident), their registries are their
  own, and `Registries::None` says so.
* `modern::play` gates the layout differences by `Gen`: `entity_teleport` before
  1.21.3, the SpawnInfo sea level from 1.21.3, the reordered player-position
  packet from 1.21.3, the quantized `lpVec3` velocity from 1.21.9, the pose
  meta serializer moving 21 → 20 in 1.21.9, attribute-id translation and the
  1.20.5 UUID modifier id, and the old `add_entity` trailing-short velocity.
  `write_stack` now writes a compat stand-in under the real item's name.
* Each old codec keeps its own login and chunk codec (those genuinely differ),
  but delegates every other event to `modern::Codec(version()).encode` and every
  serverbound packet it does not itself decode to
  `modern::Codec(version()).decode`, and reports `full_gameplay()` /
  `supports_containers()` true, plus `block_for_item` and `resolve_reported_item`.

Tests: `protocol::modern::play` (old add_entity velocity, teleport packet,
pose serializer), `protocol` (766–773 full_gameplay, spear residence),
`v767` (full-game assertions, gameplay packets through the fallback, teleport
layout). The J4 spear test on v767 still passes.

## Not done / limits

* **Point releases sharing one protocol id** (1.21.2/1.21.3, 1.21.7/1.21.8,
  1.21.9/1.21.10) get the later release's entity/attribute ids where they
  differ; `minecraft-data` has one dump per id.
* **Explosion particles are not sent** on these codecs (the packet was rebuilt
  in 1.21.9 and the older particle registry is not available here; the event is
  cosmetic).
* **The static tags packet is not sent**, unchanged from before this task, so
  water and `climbable` behave as on the other old codecs.
* 1.20.2–1.20.4 (764/765) and older still keep the subset — a different queue's
  scope.

## Review fixes (docs/tasks/QO-review-1.md)

Five confirmed defects, each fixed in its own commit with a test:

* **J9-fix1** — 1.21.3–1.21.10 sent `entity_teleport` with the pre-1.21.2
  body. Dropped the hand-rolled `EntityMove` arm; the shared path switches to
  `entity_position_sync` (explicit deltas, f32 angles) from 1.21.3 on.
* **J9-fix2** — the old codecs' hard-coded `PLAYER_ENTITY_TYPE` was 147 in
  1.21.2/1.21.3 (needs 148) and 155 in 1.21.9 (needs 151). Dropped the
  hand-rolled `SpawnPlayer`; the generated table is used.
* **J9-fix3** — the damage-type capture dropped message ids containing `.`/`_`
  (`player_explosion`, `sonic_boom`, `mace_smash`), shifting every later id.
  Fixed the regex, added a count assertion, regenerated.
* **J9-fix4** — `Time` wrote `tickDayTime` before 1.21.2; now gated.
* **J9-fix5** — the drop path used the raw wire id; now through
  `play::write_stack`, so a dropped spear keeps its trident disguise.

## Checks

`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -j4 --
-D warnings`, `cargo test -p aether-server` (771 passed, including the five
fix tests) all clean.
